subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which parts of the #35203 multi-agent collaboration stack belong in OpenClaw core/plugin APIs versus ClawHub plugins, and which storage/security boundary should be designed first?
rationale: The request spans core routing, memory/session visibility, persisted state, config defaults, cost governance, and plugin boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product/API shape.

options.title: Keep canonical and split design work
options.body: Keep #35203 open as the canonical RFC, then split capability metadata, blackboard storage/privacy, memory promotion, and budget enforcement into separate owner-reviewed design issues before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor one narrow core primitive
options.body: Approve a first core primitive such as capability metadata in agents_list or budget preflight, leaving blackboard and memory promotion deferred until security design is settled.

options.title: Route implementation plugin-first
options.body: Treat the stack as plugin/ClawHub work and keep core limited to missing extension hooks surfaced by plugin prototypes.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and split design work
recommendation.body: Keep #35203 open as the canonical RFC, then split capability metadata, blackboard storage/privacy, memory promotion, and budget enforcement into separate owner-reviewed design issues before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest evidence for the product-boundary decision is steipete's prior scoping review on the related heavy-orchestration issue and recent merges around the affected agent surfaces.
